newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian c.bank to decide on Tauras next week.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian c.bank to decide on Tauras next week.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank said on Thursday that it will decide the fate of troubled Tauras Bank next week.
"The decision on Tauras Bank will be taken next week after official auditing results are available," the central bank said in a statement.
Options include the launching of bankruptcy proceedings if the bank, which is one of smallest of the country's 12 banks, is found to be insolvent.
The central bank removed the board of Tauras Bank earlier this month and imposed restrictions on most of its activities after it ran into liqudity problems.
The bank's president, Genadijus Konopliovas, was found dead on Monday with a bullet wound to the head. Police suspect he killed himself.
Konopliovas was one of the main owners of the bank.
The bank admitted last month that it was having serious liquidity problems and was pinning its hopes on a 40 million litas share issue.
Lithuania was rocked by a banking crisis in late 1995 with the shock closure of two of its top banks but analysts say the sector has recovered and do not expect Tauras' troubles to spread.
The bank has a limited number of corporate and business clients and so the political impact of its problems has been minimised.
